entries.title: Making Every Electron Count: The Rise Of The SmartGrid
entries.quote: In 2009, SmartGrid companies may generate $25 billion in revenues, and represent the biggest and fastest growing sector in the GreenTech – possibly even the entire – technology market.
entries.subject: Smart grid
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Gadgets for free!* (*subject to contract)
entries.quote: The combination of these two trends sets the scene for a significant expansion of the device subsidy model in 2009. ... In 2009, this approach is likely to be pervasive.
entries.subject: Device subsidies and bundling
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Disrupting the PC: the rise of the netbook
entries.quote: The netbook, also known as the mini-notebook, is likely to be the fastest growing PC segment in 2009. It may represent in excess of 15 percent of all portable PC sales, or roughly 25 million units.
entries.metric: netbook share of portable PC sales
entries.subject: Netbooks
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Moore's Law and risk
entries.quote: However, these trends may have caused a corresponding growth in the risk associated with information leakage and data theft.
entries.subject: Data leakage risk
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One). The section states no dated prediction; the quote is its thesis.

entries.title: The common sense of green and lean IT
entries.quote: In 2009, the aggregate volume of the world's data centers is likely to continue to grow, albeit possibly at a slower pace than in previous years. ... The latest, purpose-built data-centers should attain a power-unit effectiveness (PUE) rating of 1.2 or better.
entries.metric: PUE of new purpose-built data centers
entries.subject: Data center energy efficiency
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Downsizing the digital attic
entries.quote: In 2009, companies may halve what they spend on physical storage. Spending on new servers may increase by just 4 percent to $58 billion.
entries.subject: Enterprise data storage
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Smart Phones: How To Stay Clever In A Downturn
entries.quote: While sales growth for all mobile phones may decline to around 4 percent, smart phone growth could fall by more than 15 percentage points, to under 20 percent.
entries.subject: Smartphone shipments
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Data Ascends From The Basement To The Boardroom
entries.quote: In 2009 however, several factors are expected to raise the profile of information, catalyzing its ascension to the boardroom.
entries.subject: Telecom customer data analytics
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Digital Communication Loses Its Message
entries.quote: During 2009, on average office workers are expected to check their inboxes more than 50 times and send more than 160 messages daily, in all dedicating up to two hours each day to email.
entries.metric: daily inbox checks per office worker
entries.subject: Email overload
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: The Joys Of Disintermediation: Why Operators Should Embrace The Application Store
entries.quote: In 2009, mobile phone users are expected to download over 10 billion applications to their mobile phones.
entries.subject: Mobile apps
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Integration Unleashes Mobile Phone Convergence, Finally
entries.quote: But 2009 is likely to see a new range of mobile phones, which overcome the convergence compromise. ... Camera phones boasting high-quality lenses and 12 mega-pixel sensors are expected to offer image quality that rivals the best point-and-shoot cameras.
entries.subject: Converged mobile phones
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part One).

entries.title: Generic becomes the 'it' brand
entries.quote: In 2009, companies and consumers may actively seek out unbranded or relatively unknown technology brands on the basis that they are good enough and, more importantly, significantly cheaper
entries.subject: Unbranded technology products
entries.note: Read from an Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF. Rank is the chapter number in the full report (the earlier Mondaq entries are chapters 1 to 6 of Technology and 1 to 5 of Telecommunications).

entries.title: Social networks in the enterprise: Facebook for the Fortune 500
entries.quote: While 2009 should see a growth in ESN, it will probably only be in a minority of leading-edge firms.

entries.title: Sinners become saints
entries.quote: The volatility in the price and supply of oil, gas and coal may be a key reason for the growing supply of nuclear power, whose global generating capacity is forecast to grow by 1.3 percent in 2009 and could double by 2030
entries.subject: Nuclear power
entries.note: Read from an Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF. Rank is the chapter number in the full report (the earlier Mondaq entries are chapters 1 to 6 of Technology and 1 to 5 of Telecommunications). Forecast cited from a source (footnote 93); 'could double by 2030' is a second horizon. The chapter recasts two technologies once regarded as evils.

entries.quote: Given this context, up to one out of every ten print publications could be obliged either to reduce print frequency, cease physical printing or, in some cases, shut down entirely in 2009
entries.metric: share of print publications reducing frequency, stopping print or closing
entries.subject: Print publishing

entries.title: Mobile termination rates in Europe: a cut too far or a cut too fast?
entries.quote: That differential of $0.09 is likely to become the subject of heated debate in 2009 and winners and losers may be defined by the rate at which it declines.
entries.subject: Mobile termination rates
entries.note: Read from an Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF. Rank is the chapter number in the full report (the earlier Mondaq entries are chapters 1 to 6 of Technology and 1 to 5 of Telecommunications). Copy hosted on Deloitte Portugal's site; the report is the English-language global edition. The differential is between the average European mobile termination rate (ten cents per minute) and fixed termination.

notes: 8th edition ('the eighth year in which the Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Global TMT Industry Group published its predictions'). Published as three separate reports under the 'TMT Trends' banner. Only Part One of the Technology and Telecommunications reports was read, from Mondaq republications dated January 2009; Part Two of each and the Media report were not found. Rank restarts at 1 within each report (section). Internet Archive retry (2026-10-02): all three reports read in full from archive.org copies (ten chapters each): Technology from deloitte.com/assets/Dcom-Global, Media from Dcom-Shared Assets, Telecommunications from a Deloitte Portugal copy of the English global edition. Appended Technology 7 to 10 (entries 12 to 15), Media 1 to 10 (16 to 25), Telecommunications 6 to 10 (26 to 30).
